# `start_avi_rtmp`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start playing a recorded AVI file out through the live-stream output.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd1240 (64-bit build), StartReadAvi @0x2ef280; static analysis of app 3.3.2: CMD_START_RTMP_PLAYBACK and CMD_STOP_RTMP_PLAYBACK constants with no const-string uses (finding #361) |

Resolves the file name, then starts an AVI reading thread that decodes the file and feeds it to the stream output; it does not record a new file. A success reply only means the thread was created: the file is opened inside the worker, so a missing or unreadable file is reported later through an AviRtmp event with state fail, not in the reply. Events from the worker: state start, then complete when the frame loop ends or fail with an error code on initialisation problems (open failure 258, non-video stream or implausible size 220, output stream initialisation failure 283; replaced by 253 aborted if a stop was already requested). The app (3.3.2) defines this command name but never sends it; it only consumes the AviRtmp event. READ (dex).

Side effects: Starts the AVI reading thread and stream output. Fails if a read thread is already running or a planet stack is active.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_avi_rtmp"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array\|object | no | - | File to play, as a bare string, as the first element of an array, or as the string member name of an object. Selection happens exactly once (no recursive unwrapping). A name without a directory component is resolved under the Video directory of the image store; a recognised full image path is kept and any other path is prefixed with the image store root. The resolved path is copied into a 256-byte buffer, at most 255 bytes, so a longer path is truncated. An empty string passes validation; no length, extension or existence check is made at request time. Absent params, an empty array, a missing name, an explicit null or a non-string value give 105. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | File name absent, null, not a string, or an array whose first element is not a string | `expected string param` |
| 268 | An AVI reading thread is already running | `operation is in progress` |
| 524 | A planet stack is active | `function conflict` |
| 212 | Reading thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Failures that occur after the thread starts (file open, format, output initialisation) are delivered as AviRtmp events, not as replies.

## Example

Request, play-by-name:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"start_avi_rtmp","params":{"name":"example.avi"}}
```

Request, play-bare-string:

```json
{"id":32,"method":"start_avi_rtmp","params":"example.avi"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_avi_rtmp","result":0,"code":0,"id":31}
```

Reply, already-playing:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_avi_rtmp","error":"operation is in progress","code":268,"id":33}
```
